subject: Request fanout + throttle event — PrismPay production impact
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@prismpay.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, support@redwood.com
Cc: PrismPay SRE <sre@prismpay.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -0000
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 spike + 429s — started ~12:20 UTC

Hey Stephanie / Redwood support,

We're seeing a sharp degradation in the hosted API since ~12:20 UTC. p95 and p99 for our requests spiked, and a noticeable percentage of calls are returning 429s followed by client retries. Our product is timing out in customer checkout flows.

Quick facts:
- First observed: 12:20 UTC
- Impact: ~18% of calls get 429s over a 25 min window, p99 increased from ~1.3s to ~6.7s
- We attached a small set of traces and our API usage CSV for the window.

This is blocking a live merchant. Can someone confirm whether this is a Redwood-hosted throttling/regulator issue or something on our side? We haven't changed concurrency on our side.

Attachments: prismpay_sample_traces.ndjson, prismpay_api_usage_20260819.csv

—Ethan
Ethan Cole
Lead SRE, PrismPay
ethan.cole@prismpay.com
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@prismpay.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, support@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 13:18:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spike + 429s — started ~12:20 UTC

Thanks for flagging, Ethan — I'm investigating now and have looped in Rishi (platform infra) and Laura (customer success).

Can you confirm: were these requests coming from a single API key or multiple keys? Also does the attached usage CSV match the peaks you saw?

Immediate next steps I will coordinate:
- Rishi will look at rate-limit enforcement + request fanout patterns and whether retry amplification is visible from our side.
- We'll pull host/service traces and correlate to any automated throttles or policy rollouts.
- If this is an active outage for your customers we'll escalate internally for an exec signal.

I created HubSpot ticket PRISM-84 and pasted your traces link: https://hubspot.redwood/deal/PRISM-84.

We should have a first update in 30–45 minutes.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 13:31:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spike + 429s — started ~12:20 UTC

Stephanie — brief technical notes from platform signals (first 10m):

Observations:
- At ~12:18 UTC we see a short burst of high-concurrency requests from a set of client IPs associated with PrismPay keys. Request fanout into backend model shards increased queuing on the serving pool.
- Our rate limiter kicked in with 429 responses at the gateway layer. Client retries (exponential backoff not configured) caused repeated requests and amplified tail latencies — classic retry storm.
- p95 and p99 regressions match increased queue latency on the GPU workers; token generation times were correlated but queuing had larger contribution.
- No scheduled policy rollouts or config changes in that window from our side.

Immediate mitigation options (recommended order):
1) Temporarily raise PrismPay soft-limit by 30% on the gateway to drain the queue while we investigate. (Risk: short-term extra cost for PrismPay-only traffic.)
2) Apply a short-lived circuit-breaker for clients whose retry rate exceeds threshold (blocks noisy clients while preserving healthy flows).
3) Enable prefix KV caching for frequent prompt patterns if appropriate (medium-term).

I can make the soft-limit change now if Stephanie approves; will also open a Grafana window and a trace correlation dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/hosted/slug?orgId=1&from=1692450000000&to=1692536400000

Logs attached: selected traces + gateway rate-limiter counters.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@prismpay.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 13:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spike + 429s — started ~12:20 UTC

Ethan — update and proposed short-term mitigations: 

We identified retry amplification caused by increased concurrency + gateway rate limiting. Rishi recommends a two-step mitigation: (1) temporary raise of your soft-limits for the next 20 minutes to allow in-flight requests to drain, and (2) we will apply a short circuit-breaker to suppress high-frequency retries from repeating keys while preserving baseline throughput.

If you approve the soft-limit bump I'll make the change now (will be scoped just to PrismPay API keys). After we stabilize we'll run a controlled test with you to validate p95/p99.

Cc'ing Laura to discuss credits if there is customer impact.

—Stephanie

Thanks Stephanie — please proceed with the soft-limit bump. We'll stand by for the circuit-breaker note and will run smoke tests once you confirm. One ask: can you confirm whether Redwood will consider a service credit? This is affecting a major merchant checkout.

—Ethan
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 21:40:00 -0000
Subject: Exec update: PrismPay incident wrap and next steps

Team — a short exec-friendly summary for the incident and customer ask. Please keep this internal for now.

Summary: PrismPay experienced a 20–25 minute event on 2026-08-19 (12:18–12:45 UTC) where p95/p99 spiked and ~18% of requests returned 429s. Root cause: transient fanout combined with gateway rate-limiter + aggressive client retries, which amplified queueing on our GPU workers.

Customer impact: High — merchant checkouts degraded. PrismPay is asking for a credit; Stephanie has the customer engaged.

Actions completed:
- Rishi performed a targeted soft-limit increase during the event and applied a short circuit-breaker to throttle noisy retrying keys.
- Post-event traces captured; we've scheduled a follow-up with PrismPay SRE to walk through retry behavior and best-practice SDK guidance (to avoid tight retries).
- Product will propose default circuit-breaker settings and an alert for high client retry ratios.

Next steps (owner):
- CS/AE (Stephanie): finalize compensation conversation and timeline with customer.
- Eng (Rishi/Marcus): implement a guard in the gateway to detect retry storms and auto-scale an emergency routing fallback. Due: 2026-09-03.
- Product (Connor): ship billing policy for emergency soft-limit bumps (how to charge/credit). Due: 2026-08-30.

Please add any missing items; I'll convert to an exec memo for leadership once we have the customer's compensation decision.

—Laura
Laura Bennett | Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
